H_hierarchical.evidence: The paper groups S2-S6 as five risk-mitigation states under the contingency policy, but Fig. 10 is a flat FSM with no explicit composite parent or nested sub-FSM.

G_guards_arith.evidence: The Contingency Plan uses multi-variable guards over Safety Monitor state, flight segment, airspace, and shortest contingency route; Fig. 13 includes conjunctions and negated alternatives such as smstate=autonomousOp & inEnrouteSegment & shortestContingencyRoute != climb & != land.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: Transitions select contingency procedures, update contingencyProc, notify the Mission Manager, replace the reference trajectory, or command the Flight Termination System.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: The Safety Monitor can command flight termination at any time; CTL properties require hardEvent -> AX state=flightTermination and flightTermination to be final.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: State names and S1-S7 structure are in Sec. 7.1.1/Fig. 10, while procedure-selection actions and guards are later in Sec. 7.2.1/Fig. 13.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as flight termination, C2 link loss, geofencing, manual control, and avoidance maneuver imply aviation-specific response rules beyond simple state names.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: Actions are mostly narrative: C2 loss leads to land/climb/termination, GPS loss leads to manual/climb/loiter, traffic alert leads to avoidance, and boundary alert resumes after avoidance.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: Guards combine multiple variables and boolean structure, including smstate, inEnrouteSegment, shortestContingencyRoute, inControlledAirspace, and negated contingency predicates.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: Although risk-mitigation states are grouped conceptually, the paper does not define an explicit composite state with its own entry/during/exit behavior.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: The model requires flight termination to be reachable in one step and hard events to force transition to flightTermination from the operating/risk states.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: No deep composite state or non-trivial initial pseudo-chain is specified.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: The policy has several multi-variable boolean guards and precondition properties where SMT-style consistency checks could catch contradictory procedure enabling.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: Hard contingency and termination rules apply across many states, making a forced transition much shorter than duplicating S1-S6 to S7 edges.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: Outputs are abstract procedures such as loiter, climb, avoidance, manual control, land, and flightTermination, delegated to Mission Manager or FTS rather than concrete actuator commands.

key_nl_quotes: The occurrence of one single soft contingency can be addressed by the Contingency Manager, but any combination of nested contingencies or the occurrence of a hard event require instant flight termination.
The Contingency Manager will notify the Mission Manager to execute the selected action.
one_line_pitch: This is a hard avionics contingency-supervisor case with global termination escapes, multi-variable policy guards, and abstract mitigation actions split across architecture, narrative, and formal SMV sections.
rationale: The sample is a strong stress test because the paper gives a real contingency-management FSM plus a separate procedure-selection EFSM with contextual guards and safety properties. Its weakness for Umple-style baselines is not hierarchy but the combination of global hard-event escape paths, multi-variable guard logic, and non-trivial abstract actions such as landing, climbing, avoidance, manual-control handoff, and flight termination. The paper is detailed enough to construct a reference model and has no hard exclusion for parallel regions, history states, pure I/O wiring, or vagueness.
